questions.stem: Which of the following best defines isotopes?

options.text: Atoms of different elements with the same mass number
Atoms of different elements with the same number of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Atoms of the same element with different numbers of electrons

questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element that have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons, giving them different mass numbers.

questions.stem: Carbon-12 and Carbon-14 are isotopes. Why do they have identical chemical properties?

options.text: Because they have the same mass number
Because they have the same electron configuration
Because they are both radioactive
Because they have the same number of neutrons

questions.explanation: Isotopes have the same chemical properties because they have the same number of electrons arranged in the same way. Chemical properties depend on electron arrangement, not on the number of neutrons.

questions.stem: Chlorine has two isotopes: Cl-35 (75% abundance) and Cl-37 (25% abundance). What is the relative atomic mass of chlorine?
questions.explanation: Ar = [(35 x 75) + (37 x 25)] / 100 = [2625 + 925] / 100 = 3550 / 100 = 35.5. The relative atomic mass is closer to 35 because Cl-35 is more abundant.

questions.stem: Why are the relative atomic masses in the Periodic Table not whole numbers for most elements?

options.text: Because the values are weighted averages of the masses of different isotopes
Because neutrons have a mass slightly less than 1
Because electrons contribute a small fraction of mass
Because atoms have fractional numbers of protons

questions.explanation: Most elements exist as mixtures of isotopes with different masses. The relative atomic mass is a weighted average that takes into account the mass and abundance of each isotope.

questions.stem: Which isotope is used for carbon dating of archaeological artefacts?

options.text: Carbon-14
Carbon-12
Carbon-16
Carbon-13

questions.explanation: Carbon-14 is a radioactive isotope with a half-life of 5,730 years. By comparing the ratio of C-14 to C-12 in a sample with that in living organisms, scientists can determine the age of the artefact.

questions.stem: Hydrogen has three isotopes: protium (mass number 1), deuterium (mass number 2), and tritium (mass number 3). How many neutrons are in tritium?
questions.explanation: Neutrons = Mass number - Atomic number = 3 - 1 = 2. All hydrogen isotopes have 1 proton, but tritium has 2 neutrons, giving it a mass number of 3.

questions.stem: Which physical property differs between isotopes of the same element?

options.text: Chemical reactivity
Mass and density
Electron configuration
Bonding behaviour

questions.explanation: Isotopes differ in their physical properties such as mass and density because they have different numbers of neutrons. Their chemical properties remain the same because they have the same electron configuration.
